senses.gloss: (b. h.) light, day (opp. night); (astronomical) day; trnsf. day of life; time.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 6:9">Gen. R. s. 6</cite> <he>הי׳ והגשמים וכ׳</he> the noise of the moving light (<cite ref="Yoma 20b:10">Yoma 20ᵇ</cite> <he>קול גלגל חמה</he>) and the rains &c.; Midr. Sam. ch. IX. Gen. R. l. c. (ref. to <cite ref="Malachi 3:19">Mal. III, 19</cite>) <he>י׳ שהוא מלהט וכ׳</he> it is the day light which will glow the wicked (cmp. <cite ref="N01279"><he>נַרְתֵּק</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Moed Katan 25b:10">M. Kat. 25ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Amos 8:9">Am. VIII, 9</cite>) <he>זה יוֹמוֹ של וכ׳</he> that means the day of life of Josiah (who was slain in the bloom of manhood).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 3:9">Gen. R. s. 3</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 1:5">ib. I, 5</cite>) <he>י׳ אחד … ואיזה זה יוה״כ</he> ‘one (distinguished) day’ … that is the Day of Atonement.

<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 5:5">Ḥull. V, 5</cite> (<cite ref="Chullin 83a:16">83ᵃ</cite>) <he>הי׳ הולך וכ׳</he> the day follows the night, i.e. the beginning of the night is the beginning of the new day.
Taan. 29ᵃ, v. זַכַּאי; a. v. fr.—י׳ טוב (abbr. יו״ט) Holy Day; festival.
<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 4:1">R. Hash. IV, 1</cite>; a. fr.—
Yoma VII, 4 ויו״ט היה וכ׳ and the Highpriest gave a festival to his friends; a. fr.—Yom Tob, name of a treatise of the Tosefta (v. בֵּיצָה).—י׳ הכפורים (abbr. יו״כ, יה״כ) Day of Atonement.
Yoma I, 1; a. v. fr.—בֶּן יוֹמוֹ of the same day, not quite one day old, used on the same day.

B. Kam. 65ᵇ; a. fr.—Tanḥ. Kor. 3; ed. Bub. 6; Num. R. s. 18 תינוקות בְּנֵי יוֹמָן (not בן) children just born; a. fr.—Du. יוֹמַיִם. Mekh. Mishp., N’zikin, s. 7; B. Kam. 90ᵃ ישנו בדין יום או י׳ comes under the law of ‘one or two days’ (Ex. XXI, 21) ; B. Bath. 50ᵃ.—Mekh. l. c. יום שהוא כי׳ וי׳ שהוא כיום a time which counts like two days, and two days which count like a day, which is twenty four hours (from the time of the accident, including part of this and part of the next day).—

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 65b:15">Snh. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>מה יום מיומים</he> (Ms. M. a. Rashi <he>מה היום וכ׳</he>) what difference is there between to-day (Sabbath) and the next day?; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 11:10">Gen. R. s. 11</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 918:4">Yalk. Deut. 918</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 617:8">Yalk. Lev. 617</cite>.—Pl. <cite ref="J00410"><he>יָמִים</he></cite>; constr. <cite ref="J00409"><he>יְמֵי</he></cite>, <cite ref="J00407"><he>יְמוֹת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 3:6">Erub. III, 6</cite> <he>לשני י׳</he> for both days.
<cite ref="Mishnah Zevachim 5:7">Zeb. V, 7</cite> <he>לשני י׳</he> during two days and one night.
<cite ref="Pesachim 52a:4">Pes. 52ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>שני י׳ טובים של גליות</he>, v. <cite ref="C00919"><he>גָּלוּת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 4:8">Taan. IV, 8</cite> <he>לא היו י׳ ט׳ וכ׳</he> Israel had no days as merry as &c.; a. fr.—
Ab. I, 17, a. fr. כל יָמַי all my lifetime.—Esp. יְמוֹת season, period of. י׳ הגשמים, v. גֶּשֶׁם I.—י׳ החמה
Gen. R. s. 33, end; a. fr.—י׳ הלבנה the lunar year.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 33:7">Ib.</cite>; a. fr.—<he>י׳ בגרות</he>, <he>י׳ נערות</he>, v. <cite ref="B00092"><he>בַּגְרוּת</he></cite> &c.
